title: COVID Alert
description: Build an educational symptom and simulated exposure-check app with clearly labelled outcomes and local history.
problem: Learners need a source-grounded way to understand and extend COVID Alert while separating implemented behavior from demo data, simulations, and missing integrations.
audience: Third-year undergraduate students who have completed introductory programming and want a practical mobile mini-project.
prerequisites: Git basics and ability to run the platform tooling described in the source README
learning_outcomes: Explain and trace check and exposureresult types, symptom catalogue, resources, and sample data in its named source files.
Explain and trace exposureservice interface, simulated implementation, and simulation labelling in its named source files.
Explain and trace weights, duplicate/unknown filtering, thresholds, advice, and disclaimer in its named source files.
Explain and trace tocheck, lastcheck, formatting, interval calculation, and empty state in its named source files.
Explain and trace provider lifecycle, asyncstorage adapter, resources screen, reusable controls, and tabs in its named source files.
Explain and trace simulation tests, storage failures, labels, disclosure, and evidence limits in its named source files.
Explain and trace screen-to-model integration, clear-state wording, limitations, and demo script in its named source files.
Distinguish unit-test evidence from device, service, and deployment evidence.
Propose a safe, bounded extension without describing it as already implemented.
